subject: Information Theory
title: Quantum Error Correction
description: A fast breakdown of Quantum Error Correction for builders.

hook.text: A qubit can't be copied—the no-cloning theorem forbids it. So how do you protect quantum information from errors?

buildup.text: Quantum errors are continuous: a qubit can rotate by any amount, not just flip. Correction seems impossible.

discovery.text: Shor's 9-qubit code spreads one logical qubit across nine physical qubits. Syndrome measurements detect errors.

twist.text: Measurement collapses quantum states—but syndromes only reveal the error type, not the data. Privacy is preserved.

climax.text: Surface codes and topological codes now lead the quest for fault-tolerant quantum computing. Error correction is key.

punchline.text: No copying. No peeking. Still correctable. Quantum magic.

quiz.question: Why is quantum error correction more challenging than classical?
options: Qubits can't be copied and errors are continuous
